items.q: Do we need WFI for our final rinse?
items.a: Only if your risk assessment says so, as is common for cerebrospinal fluid contact. For blood or lymph contact, PW with a written endotoxin limit is usual. Our package is polypropylene with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pretreatment, not WFI, pure steam, stills or stainless steel. Natural PP is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats.

items.q: Our rinse water meets USP PW. Is that enough for implants?
items.a: Not on its own. The Purified Water (PW) monograph sets no endotoxin limit, and its microbial action level (USP <1231>) is guidance only. Write both into your water specification and sample at the washer inlet.

items.q: Is the water system validated or qualified?
items.a: Qualified. You validate the cleaning process (ISO 13485:2016, 7.5.6), for example to ASTM F3127. The water system is qualified by installation and operational qualification (IQ, OQ), then performance qualification (PQ) from routine sampling.

items.q: Do you supply water for hospital reprocessing?
items.a: Our scope: [hospital water scope]. Hospital reprocessing water follows CSA Z314:23 and ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023. Critical water under ST108 is looser on ions than Purified Water, tighter on microbes, and has an endotoxin limit.
